Obtained results indicate that the proposed controller is able to significantly improve microgrids hosting capacity of variable renewable resources under frequency regulation criteria while consistently enhancing the system overall frequency regulation process.

articleTitle: Refinement in e-mobility ramp-up and impact on global grid planning
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The energy transition pushed by climate change imposes an increased pressure on power distribution grids. While the integration of new DER continues, especially the politically fostered e-mobility ramp-up and increase in heat-pumps require additional network capacities. The extend of grid expansion depends on both regulatory and technological constraints, which imply very high uncertainty in planning and budgeting. The approach presented in this paper relies as it were on a counterflow planning process in order to estimate the e-mobility load implications to the grid at best estimation and to identify priorities where to start best with detailed planning of grid expansion.

articleTitle: Expansion of the power distribution system of an existing apartment building, if necessary with energy management system for the use of charging points in the building
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: More and more households, businesses and communities are transforming themselves into self-sufficient electricity producers, which will thus be less and less dependent on the supply grid in the future. The “participants” generate and store their own electricity via renewable energy sources with the help of solar panels, wind turbines, microgrids and battery storage, which they also consume themselves or even sell when needed. The effective use of renewable energy is the opportunity, for use in buildings, for charging vehicles while reducing CO2 emissions. Electricity generation is changing, and so is the way we store, consume and manage electricity. New technologies allow us to use our “buildings as a grid”. Transport is changing, and as more and more e-vehicles are on the road, we need to charge them efficiently without overloading the electricity grids. However, building owners face challenges in doing so, as the given infrastructure of years to decades ago does not meet the requirements needed today and, in the future, to incorporate e-mobility into everyday life and thus into existing buildings.

articleTitle: Simulation of the impact of EV penetration on electrical grids in Portugal
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: With the progressive increase in the purchase of electric vehicles (EV), including hybrids, there is also an increase in energy consumption in homes and greater demand at public charging stations. A profile of domestic consumption and a secondary substation (SS) in Porto were considered to analyse the impact of EV charging. Depending on the number of EVs, charging in homes implies increased energy consumption and possible constraints on the network, such as overloads and blackouts. To face these restrictions, a solar energy simulation system was created, by photovoltaic panels (PV), and considered the storage of this energy in a battery (ES) that will be used to reduce the excessive consumption of charges. In the case of SS, the number of EVs to be charged will have to be much higher than in households for any impact on the network to be observed, and to ensure that there is no grid overload, load scenarios distributed over the time horizon and off-peak hours were studied.

articleTitle: E-Mobility integration through smart charging – E-Redes case study
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: E-REDES, Portugal's mainland distribution system operator (DSO), is currently equipping its office buildings throughout Portugal with charging infrastructure. Many of these locations have insufficient grid capacity to accommodate the required number of charge stations. The same will happen for many grid connection sites, whether it'll be apartment complexes, dwellings, or office buildings.To prepare the grid for the increase of Electric Vehicles (EV), E-REDES started a project to test smart charging technology at its office in Setúbal, in collaboration with the Dutch company GreenFlux.With this project, E-REDES is learning how to promote smart charging as a network management tool and how it can be used in flexibility markets. The experience and data of this project are already being used in other projects and to study the regulatory framework that'll allow for the dissemination of smart charging on the grid.

articleTitle: Evaluation of potential electric vehicles charging flexibility on LV network's operation as a part of distribution network planning
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Loads with higher-rated powers and stochastic behaviour, such as charging points for electric vehicles, are increasingly being connected to modern distribution networks. Due to their stochastic behaviour, their consumption is difficult to predict. Their consumption can lead to the overloading of network elements, increase network losses and cause problems with the power quality. Conventional concepts of network planning usually do not consider the potential flexibility of electric vehicle charging which could affect network conditions and could lead to unnecessary investments in the network and network oversizing. With the proposed methodology, an individual operator of the distribution network can evaluate the potential impact of electric vehicle charging flexibility in an individual network. The methodology is applied via a simulation platform, which allows an operator to model different kinds of loads, such as heat pump consumption or household consumption. The proposed methodology utilizes the Monte Carlo method to perform a power flow analysis allowing it to model loads with stochastic behaviour. Results indicate that there will be a substantial potential for flexibility provided by owners of electric vehicles in the future, therefore a delay of some investments will be possible if an appropriate local flexibility market is created.

articleTitle: Scalable forecasting and model predictive control for electric vehicles smart charging
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: In near future electric vehicles load may represent up to 45% of buildings energy consumption. Controlling charging will play an essential role to minimize energy costs and to contribute to grid balancing. The uncertainty regarding electric vehicles demand is the main difficulty to optimize the energy consumption of EV chargers. Novel norms regarding vehicle to grid communication interface recommend new information exchanges between vehicles and the charging facility to mitigate this uncertainty. Indeed, drivers will be able to request an energy and departure time. We present a smart charging model considering the inherent stochasticity of this energy management problem, leveraging drivers' information. We then introduce what we consider to be the most straightforward, yet efficient, method to implement a low maintenance, system agnostic and scalable smart charging system. We present numerical simulations of this controller on a real dataset of smart charging sessions and highlight the importance of forecasts.

articleTitle: Standardization or how to help the development of E-Mobility in a grid-friendly manner?
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract:
For the development of electric mobility, standardization aims to define an interoperability framework and requirements that guarantee:

)user safety, but also equipment and infrastructure protection and)

))their proper integration into the electrical system.))

Enedis has been involved in e-mobility standardization together with EDF R&D since the very beginning of e-mobility standardization to promote and find the best way for e-mobility's deployment while respecting the distribution electrical network.))

))This involvement in e-mobility standardization has permitted to consider grid requirements in the standards and will enable smart charging and a better integration of the e-mobility in the smart grid.

articleTitle: Consistency of harmonic emission limits for electric vehicle chargers considering vehicle to grid capabilities
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Depending on the mode of operation (e.g. charging/consuming or discharging/generating), different harmonic emission limits might apply to a single fast charger or an installation consisting of multiple fast chargers. This paper summarizes the present standardization framework for device-based and installation-based harmonic emission limits for both consuming and generating operation. Emission limits are exemplarily calculated for one fast charger and a charging installation consisting of 12 fast chargers. For the installation, a load shaving capability is also considered. Based on the results, existing inconsistencies and possible improvements are identified which can serve as inputs for the standardization groups dealing with the revisions of the respective standards and guidelines.

articleTitle: Validation of a fault level measurement algorithm for electricity networks
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: For electricity distribution networks, fault level management remains one of the greatest challenges to overcome in the transition to Net Zero. The rapid growth of low carbon technologies, such as distributed renewable generation or electric vehicles, will dramatically increase the exercising of distribution systems, potentially stressing the networks beyond the intended design. Innovative solutions that enable active fault level management are therefore essential for network operators to ensure any fault current remains within safe design limits, by obtaining high quality data of network characteristics. The Real Time Fault Level Monitor (RTFLM) is an attractive solution to enable electricity Distribution Network Operators (DNOs) worldwide to safely accept new connections, potentially without or by reducing/deferring the need for disruptive and costly network reinforcement. This paper discusses Outram Research's development of the RTFLM device, with particular emphasis on the rigorous testing that has been completed to date with two UK DNOs, SP Energy Networks and UK Power Networks, and explores the benefits of deploying this technology to overcome the fault level challenges associated with Net Zero.

articleTitle: An innovative method for detecting transformer air leaks
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Oxygen is one of the main components that, together with heat, moisture and acids, cause degradation of the insulation paper, shortening the lifetime of the transformer. To minimize the amount of oxygen in the transformer tank, it should be protected against ambient air ingress. This is commonly done using a membrane or rubber bag sealed transformer design. However, air leaks do occur for a variety of reasons, and it is important to detect them and to perform corrective actions to minimize paper degradation and extend the transformer's lifetime. The authors present in this paper how air ingress can be detected already in its early stages by measuring the total pressure of all gases dissolved in oil, where, in case of an air leak, nitrogen and oxygen are the main components. The main parts of the method are efficient gas extraction with vacuum and pressure measurement under stable and controlled conditions. Pressure sensors represent mature and very robust technology and provide good sensitivity. The paper presents a few actual case studies of well-sealed transformers, one with an active air ingress issue, and for comparison, a free-breathing transformer after degassing its oil.

articleTitle: A large-scale comparison of the grid impact of centralized and decentralized charge control for electric vehicles
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The global goal for a significant reduction of carbon emissions in the mobility sector is accompanied by an increasing market penetration of electric vehicles (EV). As a result of this, distribution grids see a change in power demand. This contribution investigates and compares different decentralized and centralized EV charging control approaches with respect to their grid impacts and user satisfaction. The focus of this analysis is the utilization of different types of reactive power management using heuristic problem optimization for chargers. A large-scale MV and LV grid simulation framework is developed and combined with an EV simulation. Parameters such as transformer and line loading, losses, voltage profiles and voltage band violations as well as the reached fleet state of charge (SOC) are considered. The comparison of the implemented scenarios shows that a decentralized reactive power injection combined with potential active power curtailment results in the best EV integration.

articleTitle: The introduction of low voltage DER protective device in Korea
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Due to the increased DERs (Distributed Energy Resources) in the electric power distribution system. There so many problems, such as instability of power quality, increase of safety risk by islanding and the difficulty in coordination protection and so on. Especially, the problem of voltage rise and islanding in electric power distribution system is the concern in KOREA. This paper introduces that DERMS (Distributed Energy Resource Management System) which is being constructed for the voltage and active power and antiislanding. Particularly the detection and protection performance of islanding is described in detail including the various verification cases of the system in field test.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the use of electric vehicles for the provision of ancilary services to support microgrids operation under fault conditions
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: This work presents the use of a fleet of electric vehicles being used to provide support during the occurrence of faults, when the microgrid operates in islanded mode. The results indicate that the supply of power by EVs (an operation strategy using the V2G concept), mainly during fault events such as short circuits, can help to maintain the frequency within operational limits and avoid the disconnection of sensitive loads, inverters and other equipment or DERs internal to the microgrid.

articleTitle: Simulation of strategic bidding for battery storage and e-mobility in local flexibility markets with multi-agent reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-agent reinforcement learning model to simulate the bidding behavior of battery storages and electric vehicles in a bi-level market model, consisting of zonal market and a consecutive local flexibility market. The grid user behavior is computed by a multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm. Exemplary results demonstrate the functionality of the implemented model for six agents. The results show, that the model is able to outperform analytical optimization approaches by learning to use strategic bidding to exploit the potentials at the local flexibility market. Further results indicate that the presented model is capable of exploring gaming strategies to maximize the reward. We further prove the necessity of implementing a multi-agent deep reinforcement algorithm by showing that the policy computation fails when a single agent deep reinforcement learning algorithm is used for each agent independently. Using multi-agent deep reinforcement learning, we can address the non-stationarity caused by interaction of agents in the bi-level market structure.

articleTitle: Interconnected network protection systems - the basis for the reliable and safe operation of distribution grids with a high penetration of renewable energies and electric vehicles
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Power grids are increasingly faced with the introduction of decentralized, highly volatile power supplies from renewable energies and high loads occurring from emobility. However, today's static grid protection cannot manage all upcoming conditions while providing a high level of dependability and security. It forms a bottleneck of a future decarbonizing grid development.In our research project, we develop and verify an adaptive grid protection algorithm. It calculates situation dependent protection parameters for the event of power flow shifts and topology changes caused by volatile power supplies due to the increase of renewable generation and the rapid expansion of e-mobility. As a result the distribution grid can be operated with the optimally adapted protection parameters and functions for changing operating states. To safely adjust the values on protection hardware in the field, i.e., safe from hardware failures and cyberattacks, we research resilient and secure communication concepts for the adaptive and interconnected grid protection system. Finally, we validate our concept and system by demonstrations in the laboratory and field tests.

articleTitle: Optimal sizing of stationary battery storage taking into account indirect flexibility in tertiary buildings: use case of an electric vehicle community
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: This article proposes a method for taking into account the indirect flexibility (charging of Electric Vehicles) available in buildings for the sizing of stationary battery storage systems (direct flexibility). A Linear Programming approach was applied to data sourced from the Predis-MHI platform (a living lab) such that the day-to-day charging of EVs, as well as the scheduling of the charging and discharging of the proposed battery, were optimized whilst simultaneously dimensioning the battery capacity. Our results indicate that based on the percentage increase in self-consumption with reference to the base case, it is possible to reduce the battery capacity required by up to 100% as compared to a methodology that doesn't account for the indirect flexibility. Whilst relevant, the sizing approach proposed in this article assumes optimal human behavior, which is usually difficult to achieve. Our proposed approach can be adapted and used for the dimensioning of direct flexibilities for both residential and commercial/public buildings.

articleTitle: Predictive energy management in an electric vehicle charging station
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: This paper describes an energy management system (EMS) based on photovoltaic (PV) production forecasts to optimize energy flows in a microgrid. The microgrid is composed of 6 electric vehicles (EV), battery, and a PV production system. The goal is to maximize EV charging while considering moments of PV non-production. The proposed EMS is composed of two elements: a deep-learning model using LSTM to forecast PV production and a rule-based algorithm to dispatch power flow in the microgrid. The simulation findings reveal that the proposed power management system is capable of greatly increasing the state of charge (SOC) of EVs while anticipating times of PV non-generation. Four scenarios were run over different prediction periods to show the benefit of forecasting on energy management. A total benefit of 9.49% on the total state of charge (SOC) of EVs charged with a 60-minute forecast compared to management without PV forecast.

articleTitle: Introduction of network tariffs for e-mobility-first experiences in the municipality of Zurich
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Zurich's distribution system operator (DSO) ewz observed a strong increase in E-mobility in its supply area, from 2 MW of installed capacity in 2016 to ca. 30 MW in 2021. The additional load peaks from charging stations coincide with existing load peaks of the city of Zurich, which may pose a problem in the future with an even higher density of E-mobility. Therefore, ewz introduced a Demand Side Response (DSR) scheme in 2020, by implementing time fixed network tariffs for E-mobility to set incentives to the end-customers to reduce peak loads. Two years after the introduction of the new tariff schemes, we present first conclusions on the effects, both for ewz as DSO and for end-customers. Load profiles from about 400 smart meters of 2'500 charging stations, divided into customer groups, were evaluated. Our analysis shows a clear sensitivity of end-users to special tariffs for Emobility. It can be stated that generally, price incentives are working. Results show that customer groups have reacted differently to the E-mobility tariffs. In particular, the tariff which includes a capacity charge has an impact on the load behaviour of commercial charging stations during lunch time. The change in charging behaviour reduces load peaks of E-Mobility and can lead to financial savings for customers. The results of ewz E-Mobility tariffs should be regarded as a first step in untapping the potential of demand flexibility for ewz as DSO, end-customers and market participants.

articleTitle: Generation of optimized schedules of a charging process under the application of dynamic electricity tariffs and self-consumption optimization
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: This paper describes a way to implement an optimized operational behavior for charging processes in the field of e-mobility by automatically generating load profiles. The presented concept aims at adapting the power supply to the volatile renewable energy generation in the power system. By automatically adjusting load profiles, electricity customers will optimize their electricity consumption in the future to promote the integration of renewable energies and minimize their electricity procurement costs. In addition, the power grids are relieved locally by realizing a synchronization of the load profile with the customer's power generation. In this context, a concept for applying self-consumption optimization and price differences through a dynamic electricity tariff is provided for the electricity customer. The present work deals with a data model relevant for automated control based on the abovementioned criteria. Based on an annual simulation of the customer's economic potential, it is shown that the optimized mode of operation can significantly reduce the electricity procurement costs of a charging process.

articleTitle: Flexibility assessment of e-mobilty in multi-energy districts
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The future energy districts are expected to have an increasing level of integration between different energy carriers. Different sectors such as power, heating and cooling as well as transport will be coupled through conversion and storage technologies. This work aims to assess the flexibility of e-mobility in a multi-energy district. An e-mobility module is developed and integrated into the Ehub optimization tool. The optimal operation of electric vehicles is a function of the overall multi-energy system boundary conditions given by the available supply and demand and the set objectives to minimize costs and CO2 emissions. Using a hypothetical case study this work demonstrates the effect of e-mobility on supply and demand-side flexibility in the multi-energy district.

articleTitle: Flexibility-based improved energy hub model for multi-energy distribution systems
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The increasing integration of variable wind generation has aggravated the imbalance between electricity supply and demand. Power-to-hydrogen (P2H) is a promising solution to balance supply and demand in a variable power grid, in which excess wind power is converted into hydrogen via electrolysis and stored for later use. In this study, an energy hub (EH) with both a P2H facility (electrolyzer) and a gas-to-power (G2P) facility (hydrogen gas turbine) is proposed to accommodate a high penetration of renewable energy. The EH is modeled and integrated into a demand response problem to mitigate voltage violations and overloads. The optimization problem is solved by a reinforcement learning method. A case study is presented to validate the proposed model and elaborate on the flexibility potential of integrating P2H into an MV CIGRE power distribution network with solar and wind sources.

articleTitle: Real-time inertia estimation in an inverter-dominated distribution grid using a physics-informed recurrent neural network
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: To ensure frequency stability, estimation of system inertia becomes essential in modern power grids. Growing shares of virtual inertia from inverter-coupled resources (ICRs) shift this task to the distribution grids (DGs) and introduce new challenges. Using a physics-informed neural network (PINN) to combine data-driven modelling with knowledge of system dynamics, this study presents an approach to real-time system inertia estimation in inverter-dominated DGs. Based on the PINN literature framework, a modified loss function (LF) with adaptive weighting is proposed for a recurrent PINN. The approach is evaluated on a 14-bus medium voltage (MV) DG model, featuring virtual inertia from distributed ICRs with characteristic nonlinearities.

articleTitle: High-power-charging: integration strategy in low-voltage grids using battery storage system
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: High-Power-Charging (HPC) can make a significant con-tribution to the provision of efficient public charing infra-structure. Currently, HPC is typically located on transport axes - connected to the medium voltage level. In the low-voltage grid, however, the operation of HPC is challeng-ing due to low grid capacities. The objective of the work behind this paper is therefore to develop a strategy for the integration of HPC into the low voltage grid. For this pur-pose, an urban distribution grid was modelled in MatPower. HPC infrastructure and a battery storage sys-tem are simulated using time series and dynamic models. Load flow calculations are used to identify the potentials and grid effects of HPC in the low-voltage grid. Subse-quently, a battery storage system is dimensioned to pro-vide energy to the HPC infrastructure. The simulation re-sults show that HPC can in principle be integrated into the low-voltage grid, but that a battery storage system should be installed at HPC locations distant from the transformer.

articleTitle: Development of a measurement-based algorithm for topology detection in distribution grids
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The current integration of electric vehicles into the low- and medium-voltage grid causes the possibility of voltage violations and thermal overloads in the grid. To recognise such violations, knowledge of the grid state is required. A necessity for obtaining the grid state is knowledge of the grid topology. However, in most distribution grids, no communication of the status of switches to gain knowledge of the grid topology takes place. Thus, algorithms to detect the topology of a distribution grid are required. This paper presents a measurement-based approach to detect topology changes in observable distribution grids of arbitrary structure and updates their topology. The algorithm consists of two steps: The identification and the validation of potential topology changes. It is shown that the algorithm is able to detect topology changes in distribution grids and provides the basis for application in research of the institute of energy systems, energy efficiency and energy economics (ie3) at TU Dortmund University.

articleTitle: Assure charge: a data driven approach to servicing and maintaining EV charge points
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The reliability of Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) is a critical factor in the widespread adoption of EVs to meet decarbonisation targets. The Assure Charge project has identified several key areas for improving EVSE reliability, particularly the need for more clearly defined roles and responsibilities in maintaining EVSE and the need for the sharing of data between charge point operators (CPOs) and third parties to provide services such as fault diagnosis and performance reporting. The project has demonstrated a fault diagnostics and job matching platform for EVSE repair on a set of public on street chargers. Using such platforms, EVSE faults can be diagnosed and often remotely repaired to reduce potential inconvenience to EV users and improve their charging experience.

articleTitle: Probabilistic EV impact: E-REDES case study using typical low voltage grids
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The energy transition is expected to lead to a significant power peak increase in LV grids. In this study, E-REDES analyses the impact of different EV charger types (residential, public and business) with two different EV charging scenarios (dumb peak charging/smart off-peak charging) along with PV penetration on two LV fictitious representative grids of a suburban and urban grid. This study plans the impact for the year 2050, with threeyear intervals, with increasing power consumption and EV and PV expected penetration rates.

articleTitle: Developmenet and field test result of real-time analysis for power distribution system in kepco-adms
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: In this paper, the development of K-ADMS (KEPCO Advanced Distribution Management System) and field test result of real-time analysis is introduced. The K-ADMS offers new opportunities to improve the efficiency of operating and controlling the distribution systems through the accurate information of the real-time situation on the network and various optimization software to handle the circumstance of network efficiently. Now a day, there are many DER (Distributed Energy Resource) interconnected to distribution network in Korea. Those DER may harm the operation of distribution network such a voltage, bidirection active power flow as utility knows that. So, the function of K-ADMS is focused on the real-time network analysis, to get more accurate information on voltage and load flow, and optimization of voltage and active power by ESS and controllable DER.

articleTitle: Charging potential of V4G through V2G standard protocol for CCS
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The eVIP (Energy Visualisation Integration and Prediction) project aims to predict the load curve of electric vehicles in a semi-private context related to hotels and restaurants. Using the gradient boosted tree algorithm, it is possible to predict the consumption of a hotel with an accuracy of approximately 83.8% with nonintrusive devices. By using this prediction and the data collected when an electric vehicle is being charged at the hotel's charging station, the peak consumption of the hotel can be optimized.We have also opened the way for V4G (Vehicle for Grid) to allow bi-directional energy flows in this semi-private micro-grid and propose flexibility services to Distribution System Operators (DSO).

articleTitle: Potential of electric vehicles to support a temporary local emergency power back-up supply in case of a large-scale blackout
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: This paper depicts the potential of electric vehicles (EVs) to provide decentral local storage capacities to a tempo-rary local emergency power back-up subnetwork within the distribution grid. The aim is to increase the overall re-silience of the electricity supply in case of a longer-lasting large-scale blackout. One of the prerequisites for operat-ing such subnetworks is to maintain local balances of ac-tive and reactive power. Therefore, a case study approach is introduced, that assesses the supply probability of local loads in multiple real MV subnetworks located in Northern Germany. In addition, the impact of a growing EV pene-tration rate (PR) is conducted. The results show that EV batteries increase the local supply probability for the EV owner itself as well as for the entire subnetwork by up to 10% in the case study region. However, the improvements are limited by the amount of locally available surplus gen-eration, which is required to charge the EV batteries and thus be available in times without power generation.

articleTitle: Setting up and scaling up an LV management system today for the future challenges of EV integration in distribution grids
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: In order to reach the ambitious goal of climate neutrality, most studies prognose an exponential increase of electric vehicles (EV) in the next two decades. This will result in a huge impact on distribution grids. To cope with it, DSOs need a variety of methods – conventional and digital – to optimize, control and expand electrical grids. These must be developed and rolled out from today on to be implemented in local grids according to the forecasts. Therefore, Westnetz set up a management system for intelligent LV grid operation on large scale that will be expanded in the next years. With this system, especially EV integration by observation and control of flexibility is made manageable.

articleTitle: Upgrading low-voltage network models for power quality investigations with a focus on voltage unbalance
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: An increasing number of high-power devices in low-voltage distribution grids, such as electric vehicles, can cause a significant decrease in power quality. For simulative investigations of the impact of future network usage, valid simulation models of low-voltage networks are necessary. A network model generator has been used to create such network models. Those models have been extended by zero-sequence parameters to allow the simulation of unbalanced load situations. The models have been validated by building the model of a field test network and by using measurement data obtained in field measurements. A final comparison with well-esta

articleTitle: Time characterization of fast variation disturbances generated by EV chargers
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: In the coming years, e-mobility will play a key role in the decarbonization of the transport of passengers and goods. This will involve the massive implementation of electric vehicle charging points which will be connected to the low voltage grid. These devices are not neutral from the point of view of electromagnetic interferences, since they inject numerous disturbances into the propagation medium. This paper is focused on the fast amplitude variations of non-intentional emission over time generated by inverters of electric vehicle chargers in the low voltage grid. This work has three main contributions. Firstly, it shows representative occurrences of fast variation of nonintentional emissions during the charging process of a commercial electric vehicle. Secondly, it demonstrates the need of characterizing the variations in the time domain, due to their high amplitude. Lastly, results demonstrate that a statistical analysis and a selection of the appropriate metrics is needed to characterize the behaviour and nature of these variations.

articleTitle: Dynamic pricing model for fast charging stations
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: This article proposes a Dynamic Pricing model for Fast Charging Stations to guide the behavior of drivers through dynamics prices. With the model, it is possible to encourage the uniform distribution of electric vehicles at charging stations, avoiding queue formation and underutilization. Dynamic charging prices encourage recharge at stations that have renewable energy generation in addition to providing more attractive charging prices outside peak demand hours, contributing to grid stability and benefiting all stakeholders.

articleTitle: Implementation of E-mobility and renewable energies in existing neighbourhoods with reference to legal requirements
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: As of today, the existing building infrastructure, mainly in older neighbourhoods (>3 years), is not designed for the provision of e-mobility. Load peaks at certain peak times put a strain on the power grid, its quality and thus the security of supply of the resource electricity, the population. Therefore, the question rightly arises: is a blackout pre-programmed by electrification? In addition, the increasing number of renewable energy components in the infrastructure, for example solar plants, photovoltaic plants, wind turbines and battery storage systems, puts a strain on the electricity grid. This statement may sound controversial in the first place, but the “small” generators are primarily distributed in the low-voltage level and thus cannot be controlled by the energy supplier; moreover, as the electricity flows bidirectionally, the power lines are heavily stressed. The “new” grid is a complex network of prosumers: Consumers who generate their own electricity on site and consume it as needed or feed it back into the grid even when there is a surplus. The issue of the availability of renewable energies have also not be overlooked in the whole complex.

articleTitle: Calculation of aggregated flexibility of an EV fleet: case study of Bornholm, Denmark
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The increased electrification of the energy sector is expected to create congestion prone operational incidents and flexibility on the power systems can be used to avoid overestimation of grid parameters and reinforcements. In particular, the transformation of the transport sector provides an opportunity through the advent of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology allows for EVs to be more than flexible loads, but also can provide energy to the grid, if connected for longer time periods. The present paper proposes a flexibility definition which allows the calculation of positive and negative flexibility that the flexibility provider can offer to mitigate congestion. This methodology is developed under the BD4OPEM H2020 project and applied to the Danish pilot, Nuvve.

articleTitle: An enhanced virtual power plant for flexibilty services into a local area (including EV's)
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Aggregation by Virtual Power Plants to provide flexibility to distribution and transmission networks is seen as an important element in the transition to Net-zero. This paper presents work carried out in the SIES 2022 ERA-Net project, which is investigating in detail the possible provision of flexibility by different technologies, including EVs, but thorough a lens of different business models. Thus, presented work relies on the real use cases. The focus of this work is on the construction of grid representations to guide bidding in potential flexibility markets. It shows that without an appropriate level of detail on the wider grid connections, these bidding strategies, and therefore associated asset optimization schedules, could lead to errors. A methodology that derives EV price response curves is highlighted, with an aim to use such curves in sophisticated optimization scheduling module for further work in management of EV integration.

articleTitle: Electrical vehicles - grid integration issues and solutions
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The EUniversal project aims to facilitate the use of flexibility services and to link distribution system's active management with electricity markets. In the framework of this project and based on optimal power flow simulations, the paper assesses the available flexibility of distributed generation and new loads, and their impact on operational planning of the electricity network under different conditions. In particular, it highlights the important role flexibility provided by electrical vehicles can play. More generally, it contributes to the question on how to design local flexibility markets, in terms of product definition and market delineation.

articleTitle: Survey results on high power charging in low voltage grids
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: To advance the electrification of the transport sector, it is essential to develop innovative charging solutions for electric vehicles and to expand the existing charging infra-structure comprehensively. In this context, the HPC-ukf project is investigating the possibilities of a low-voltage connection for high-power charging systems. A high-power charging system supplies a high amount of energy to an electric vehicle in a short time, which increases the charging speed. Due to the high power demand, it is usually installed in the medium voltage. However, this slows down a comprehensive expansion. If installed in the low voltage, it naturally leads to more grid congestions. Therefore, alternative solutions need to be considered, such as the additional use of battery storage systems. In that regard, this paper provides the basis for the HPC-ukf project by investigating the need for a high-power charging system in the low voltage and identifying essential requirements based on a stakeholder survey. The survey interviews 35 stakeholders involved in the operation of electric grids, electric vehicle fleets or charging stations. In addition, 159 electric vehicle users are polled. Based on the survey, the experience and needs of the participants are identified and requirements for high-power charging in the low voltage grid are derived.

articleTitle: Multi-flexibility electric vehicles integration model in distribution networks
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The prevalence of electric vehicles (EVs) poses significant challenges to the planning and operation of distribution networks. This paper proposes a novel EV accommodating model for distribution network operators (DNOs) to integrate EVs with multiple flexibility attributes efficiently into distribution networks. This model takes advantage of existing underutilized network assets in distribution networks to offer special services to single flexibility EV customers or heterogeneous flexibilities EV customers. By unlocking the spare network capacity, not only can EVs with various flexibilities be integrated into networks reasonably, but also the network resources utilization can be improved. Meanwhile, the network reliability to the existing fixed customers can be guaranteed. Furthermore, the services provided to EVs are cost-efficient and time-saving. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted to validate the proposed model, and results exposit that network resources can be exploited more efficiently with higher EV penetration.

articleTitle: Anticipating the development of electric road systems and their powering through the distribution grid
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: This paper presents a study led by both EDF R&D and ENEDIS. It evaluates the impact of electric highways on distribution grids, considering it only supplies heavy goods vehicles, in both traffic directions.First, we evaluate the linear power required to supply electric highways using a simplified approach. A maximum of 4 MW/km for both traffic flows is obtained. A spatial analysis of the Paris region is carried out considering this value. Results show that supplying electric highways through MV distribution grids is possible but may require some grid reinforcements that should be considered by future electric highway operators. Then, we compare from a MV distribution grid point of view the best technic and economic solution between AC and DC architectures to supply e-mobility. A specific section of A13 highway is studied. In this case, DC solutions are not beneficial to the grid operator since distances to the primary substations are too short. This conclusion may change in more rural areas where distances to the grid lengthen.

articleTitle: Cross-border flexibility prequalification of DER and EVS based on decentralised communication mechanisms for the distribution system operation
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The adoption of battery-powered electric vehicles in the EU is expected to grow to 30-40 million by 2030. This, together with the large adoption of other Distributed Energy Resources (DERs), represents a great challenge for Distribution System Operators (DSOs) in multiple perspectives, such as providing the needed charging infrastructure and ensuring that everyone is served with the expected Quality of Service (QoS), by having a secure and reliable system operation capable of mitigating grid congestion and voltage violation events. One of the mechanisms to mitigate these events can be the usage of these DER, such as Electric Vehicles (EVs), as flexibility sources for the improvement of the planning and operation of power distribution systems. This paper proposes harmonising the coordination of the prequalification process for flexibility provision (product and grid prequalification) among System and Market Operators from Portugal, Spain and France, enabling the participation of flexibility providers in multiple markets from cross-border countries through a harmonised and non-redundant prequalification process.

articleTitle: Challenges for earthing system testing at fast-charging stations
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The additional safety value regarding earthing system tests and measurements are often underrated or not properly considered during the planning phase of new construction projects or changes in electrical power systems, like fast-charging stations. The number of these charging stations is rapidly growing with the increasing popularity of e-mobility. Motorway service areas or restaurants are an attractive site for new fast-charging stations. A well designed and tested earthing system can assure personal and animal safety during phase-to-ground faults within the electrical network. To ensure that no hazardous touch-voltages appear at or in the surrounding areas of these stations, measurements according to standards like the EN 50522 [1] are performed. Within this paper we will outline the challenges of earthing system testing at such stations as well as provide you with information regarding the background of testing procedures, standards and theoretical and practical aspects.

articleTitle: False data injection attack by virtual power plants for curtailment minimization
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Studies on false data injection attacks (FDIA) against state estimation were mainly conducted on the transmission system. However, recently, as entities such as distributed energy resources (DERs), virtual power plants (VPPs), energy storage systems (ESSs), and EV charging stations, that are vulnerable to cyber-attacks, began to appear in the distribution system, research on FDIA in the distribution system is being actively conducted. Among them, this paper deals with the FDIA that VPPs attempt in the distribution system. As the number of DERs in the distribution system increases, the curtailment for DERs owned by VPP increases. This paper proposes FDIA model by VPPs to avoid curtailment considering the facts mentioned. In the model, VPPs can implement an FDIA that deceives the distribution system operator (DSO)'s state estimation with only information obtained from the DERs they own. To verify this, IEEE 33 test feeder was used and the result shows that the attack was successful without being caught in the DSO's bad data detection (BDD). This paper provides the basic concept of VPP's FDIA and shows that future DSOs need algorithms to defend against VPPs FDIA.

articleTitle: Impact analysis of EV coordinated flexibility services on active distribution networks
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The share of electric vehicles (EVs) integrated into the distribution grid has been increasing significantly over the years. By studying their behaviour, it is possible to better utilize the flexibility offered by EV through aggregation and coordination. Based on the energy requirements and vehicle availabilities at the charging station, EV charging schedules can be obtained considering multiple objectives. In this study, a mixed-integer model is developed using Python to compute the EV load profile considering different coordinated charging schemes. Using these results, the aggregated flexibility service potential of the EVs are evaluated. The execution of flexibility service and post-flexibility impacts on the grid are studied. The results show that the flexibility service implementation introduces rebound effects and the impacts can be managed using incentives and coordinated flexibility disaggregation.

articleTitle: Optimal location for EV supercharging stations directly connected to primary substations - the E-REDES/CME use case
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The presented work explores a deployment strategy for supercharging infrastructure inside urban areas near distribution grid primary substations that facilitate the large-scale introduction of EVs, supported by an optimised economic impact from grid investment and social welfare perspectives.Thinking of Electrical Vehicles (EV) supercharging facilities with power levels of 200kW or higher expected to be widely adopted and knowing that low voltage distribution grid will be insufficient to provide supercharging for multiple simultaneous charge events, a direct connection to primary substations presents as a simple and viable solution to the upcoming challenge.The proposed results support on-grid topology analysis, primary substation capacity availability, asset investment cost, and site topography viability. A multiperiod power flow is performed for each selected node to ensure that supercharging facilities connected to the same busbar with simultaneous charging sequences don't violate voltage and current profiles.Different scenarios were explored supported on the charging infrastructure (level 3 supercharges, level 2 fast charges, and combinations of other models to maximise the grid availability). Also, an optimal amount of charging capacity is being computed to cover the demographics of each area.Results are presented with a matrix that defines the required available capacity, geographical area, and grid investment to build an EV supercharging station. Analysis of the benefits and drawbacks for EV users of centralised supercharging hubs versus decentralised charging stations is also considered in this study.

articleTitle: Evaluating voltage impact due to the installation of distributed energy resources in low voltage networks
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The integration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) and Electric Vehicle Charging Points (EVCPs), in the Low Voltage (LV) networks, is creating several challenges to the Distribution System Operators (DSOs) as it may push the voltage magnitudes outside the regulated boundaries and/or increase its unbalance beyond the acceptable limits. In this paper, it is proposed a method capable of predicting the voltage impact of a new DER or EVCP installation without requiring network topology and, therefore, helping DSOs to optimise their LV networks.

articleTitle: Deploying e-mobility in the interact energy community to promote additional and valuable flexibility resources for secure and efficient grid operation
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The volatility of renewable energy sources and the increasing share of decentralised ones imply significant systemic requirements on the flexibility of Smart Grids. E-mobility can support their greater integration by offering flexibility in shaping the electricity demand curve, thereby reducing system costs and CO2 emissions. This paper deploys e-mobility in the LINK-Energy Community to promote additional and valuable flexibility resources for secure and efficient grid operation. Results show that energy communities are the most vital instrument to motivate customers to provide flexibility through e-mobility actively. They may efficiently coordinate their territory's electricity generation and charging schedules and promote carpooling between the EC members. Developing the harmonised fractal market structure with the power grid based on the holistic solution LINK creates all the conditions for the deployment of successful business models. The use case and the respective business model for the congestion alleviation - emergency driven demand response involving e-mobility are described in detail. This study shows that energy communities developed under the holistic perspective of LINK offer flexibility to the grid, even in the case of electromobility.

articleTitle: Innovative solutions to unlock grid flexibility enabled by EV charging stations: the areti experience in the platone project
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The Platone Open Framework is a flexible and secure solution that enables distribution grid flexibility/congestion management mechanisms, through innovative energy market models involving all the possible actors (DSOs, TSOs, customers, aggregators,) at many levels. The Framework is tested in different field trials one of which is developed in Rome by Areti. This paper describes the system architecture tested in the Italian demo site, highlighting the added value of the Open Framework for the DSO in integrating EVs and enabling their active contribution to grid management.

articleTitle: Methodology for planning, development and operation of power distribution systems accommodating E-mobility
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract:
DSOs (Distribution System Operators) play a key role to facilitate e-mobility as:

))Charging points are directly or indirectly connected to the distribution grid, in both cases the electricity flows through the distribution grid;))

))Clean mobility is part of energy transition at a local level, that matters to local authorities;))

))Electric mobility is an active part of smart grids, driven by innovation.))

articleTitle: Potential of a self-sufficient control for flexible loads in low voltage grids
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Due to the expansion of volatile renewable generation and the growth in the field of electric vehicles, German distribution system operators are facing new challenges. Adequate infrastructure is needed mitigating the negative impact on the power system stability. Along with these new grid actuators, consumption related capacity-bottlenecks increase. An approach is to affect the consumption behaviour. In order to replace rigid technologies such as time switches, a grid-serving load management concept is being pursued. The approach presented in this paper is based on a decentralized, self-sufficient control of flexible loads depending on the local grid status. The technological, regulatory and contractual conditions of the flexible loads in the low voltage grid, such as electric vehicles and others, are taken into account. An algorithm for decentralized control based on locally collected measurement data was developed and implemented. This approach is already being tested in a real laboratory on about hundred households in both rural and urban regions. First data from the real laboratory show a high potential of shifting and optimizing the energy consumption of flexible loads over time.

articleTitle: System wide power flow analysis of the Irish distribution network to assess the impact of projected low carbon technology loads and generation including significant increase of electric vehicles connected to the grid
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Through the Climate Action and Low Carbon Development Act 2021 the Irish Government have set out a commitment to reach net-zero emissions by 2050 and cut emissions by 51 % by 2030 compared to 2018 levels [1]. Reaching these targets will, in no small part, be attributed to the electrification of heat and transport powered by renewable generation. Today Ireland is a country of 5 million people, and there is installed capacity of about 4.5 GW of renewable generation connected to the grid. By 2030, it is projected that one million electric vehicles (EVs) will be charging on a regular basis, 600,000 homes will be heated via heat pump (HP) technology, roof top photovoltaic (PV) will be installed on hundreds of thousands of homes and there will be 5 GW of additional commercial renewable generation connected at distribution level. It is forecasted that by 2030, if unmanaged, EV load will make up approximately 28 % of the total peak demand in Ireland. ESB Networks, Irelands Distribution System Operator has established the ‘National Network, Local Connections” programme which is tasked with introducing and embedding the new systems and processes in order to facilitate the connection and operation of the new Low Carbon Technologies (LCTs), which are comprised of the EVs, HPs and PVs, and the commercial generation, while maintaining a safe, secure and reliable network. The network levels assessed under this programme include the 10 kV, 20 kV and 38 kV systems for the whole country and the 110 kV network in the Dublin area. The Network System Services (NSS) group within ESB have been tasked with analysing the Irish distribution system to identify network constraints relating to the increase in LCT usage, with the view to establish both traditional and non-traditional network solutions, such as utilising flexibility services, to maintain the integrity of the grid. ESB Networks have defined a number of LCT uptake scenarios, generation scenarios and underlying winter peak and summer night valley demand scenarios. The ESB MV distribution system model is comprised of 20 different network areas, and each of these network areas are assessed from a load flow perspective for an 11 year period from 2020 to 2030. Having carried out analysis to determine the worst-case scenario for each network area, NSS have developed network models using Siemens PSS Sincal software. NSS group are using the models to investigate the system load flows and voltage profiles, for normal and standby feeding operation of the entire distribution network for the period from 2020 to 2030. The development and utilisation of Python and VBA scripting tools to analyse and process large data sets of input data and results aids the efficiency of the large task at hand. This paper will discuss scenario modelling techniques, load flow analysis and constraint identification brought on by the changing energy landscape of the Irish distribution system.

articleTitle: E-mobility will need a different digitalization approach by DSOs, which act as energy transition facilitator: E-REDES RPA use case to agile communication with stakeholders
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Self-consumption is one pillar of the Energy Transition, which can be further exponentiated with the mobility transition to the electric vehicle. This article aims to demonstrate that the process automation, between the Portuguese Distribution System Operator (DSO) and the Portugal's Directorate-General of Energy and Geology (DGEG) that licenses electrical installations, to connect a self-consumption is a critical element that facilitates and encourages self-consumption evolution. Concluding that process automation, together with proactive monitoring and better customer relationship, have led to an exponential increase of selfconsumption production in the last two years.

articleTitle: Stability management for an increasing number of EV fast, ultra-fast and mega charging stations connected to MV network
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: In the next decades, a significant increase in the number of vehicles traditionally powered by fossil fuel is expected to make the transition to electrification. The forecasted decarbonization may have a great impact on the medium voltage (MV) distribution network, causing congestion at parts of the MV grid due to fast, ultra-fast and mega charging stations. This paper will analyze in depth the use-cases of an on-load tap changer (OLTC) distribution transformer with the aim of optimizing the existing MV distribution network. This OLTC transformer could help Distribution System Operators (DSOs) in making an active network operation strategy with dynamic load management, increasing the number of charging stations and the generation of renewable energy connected to the existing MV grid.

articleTitle: Challenges and related solutions for periodic verification of DC electric vehicle charging stations
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: For the periodic verification of DC electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) currently no standardised verification and test procedures or associating methods and protocols have been established. This belongs to the incomplete standardisation work as well as the ongoing developments of EVCS. In the course of this paper, first important approaches for possible procedures for the periodic verification of DC-EVCSs, which are already installed in the field, are presented. On the one hand, appropriately applicable sequences from existing AC test routines will be used, and on the other hand, new test procedures required in addition for DC charging stations are presented. Furthermore, a mobile high performance test device demonstrator including its functional scope is shown. Still existing questions and challenges with regard to the mentioned topic round off the article.

articleTitle: Realisation of grid-friendly charging considering usability by knowledge graph enabled explainability
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: As Smart Grids are becoming more complex and dynamic, the range of stakeholders that need to make sense of and comprehend (potentially anomalous) grid events expands beyond technical operators. For example, smart electricity grids evolve from static to dynamically changing networks of large numbers of devices, e.g., photo-voltaic units (PV), electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) etc. The slow charging of an EVCS is an event that requires an explanation for several stakeholders including the EVCS owner, customer service representatives, field engineers, grid planners. An explanation could be that overcast weather leads to lower than usual energy production through PVs in the region, this leads to a lack of supply in the grid segment and to a control intervention to reduce charging power by the grid operator. In this work we address the problem of providing explanations of events happening in a smart grid, in particular, considering a grid-friendly charging scenario.

articleTitle: Design and analysis for dynamic wireless charging infrastructure in INCIT-EV H2020 project
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Expecting future large increase of EVs infrastructure implementation to the distribution network, grid's power quality should be analyzed to ensure best performance. In INCIT-EV European project [1], companies and research laboratories work together to design solutions considering different use case studies, different types of electric vehicles and different charging solutions. This paper focus on the use case of Versailles: Dynamic wireless charging on highways (90 kW power – 80m lane – 130 km/h vehicle speed). This innovative concept will be tested on the Versailles experimental site by UGE/Vedecom/CIRCE/Enedis.

articleTitle: Harmonic and supraharmonic disturbances caused by the combined operation of fast charging stations and a battery storage
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: This paper presents a field study, in which three battery-electric vehicles were connected one after the other to a fast charging installation in a public low voltage network. The installation includes also a battery energy storage system for peak shaving purposes. One aspect of the field test was an assessment of the impact of the fast charging installation on power quality parameters such as the harmonic and supraharmonic distortion. This paper discusses both the current emission and the respective impact on the voltage disturbance levels in the network. Furthermore, the summation of harmonics is studied and the impact on voltage disturbance levels at the point of connection are compared with those at the transformer busbar, which is the point of common coupling.

articleTitle: On the predictability of scenario-based grid-load impact forecasting, using data modelling in a continuous changing context: opportunities, limitations and unforeseen implications
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Planning electricity grids is performed by models using data distributions that should reflect future reality. Increasingly the data distributions are less uniformly distributed and more fat-tailed leading to very low likelihood but high impact event. When one-in-a-million happens every year, the prediction models need to be updated and preparations need to be increased for very low likelihood but extreme impact events as these appear to become more likely.

articleTitle: CeTur, the ultimate solution for repowering concentrated urban areas
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The imminent implementation of the Electric Vehicle in cities and their decarbonization requirements creates the need of repowering the electric grid not only for EV charging, but also for the gradual replacement of traditional Aerothermal heating systems. Cities are not prepared to double or triple their future energy demand. Transformer Substations have been coexisting with the citizens since the origin of the electric grid; however, we should not have to live with their industrial aspect, noise and electromagnetic emissions, human health hazards, lack of security in maintenance and operation, etc. The typology is varied, aerial on pole, prefabricated concrete house, semi-underground and buried... All of them have their advantages and disadvantages, but the urban environment is becoming much more demanding with AGENDA 2030 taking care of its aesthetics and comfort, removing architectural barriers and of course reassuring citizens and workers welfare. All to make cities much more liveable by providing adequate and useful furniture while minimizing costs. The CeTur, due to its architectural construction in two superimposed structures, one underground and the other above ground level, dramatically reduces its occupation footprint on the track; it's multifunctional as it is capable of: housing MV and LV equipment, public/private communication equipment, EV charging equipment and static or dynamic advertising broadcast equipment through standardized 1200×1800 mm MUPI spaces or 70" LED monitors, allowing to have Return on Investment all in one. TWELCON begins to make its designs to hide urban technical equipment at the beginning of the year 2000, since then we have hundreds of units in operation for telecommunications and dozens with Transformer Substations in Spain and Portugal since 2008. We will focus this Paper on the INTERNAL/EXTERNAL DESIGN, past TESTS, SECURITY and our experience in ACCIDENTS ON THE OPERATION.

articleTitle: Distribution network operation support by demand response and dispatchable distributed renewable generators flexibility services
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Low voltage power distribution networks have undergone considerable changes in recent years. Their conventional structures of operation and control are being challenged, mainly by the large-scale integration of distributed generators based on Renewable Energy Sources and the increase in demand. In this scenario, not only new challenges appear, but also opportunities. The widespread deployment of “smart meters,” together with the desire to include citizens as fundamental players in future energy markets and system operations, through power generation or the provision of demand flexibility, is playing a key role in the new era of power systems. This work proposes a logic heuristic model working with a tool for electric power system simulation and analysis – MATPOWER – to enhance the Demand Response participation of small consumers and dispatchable distributed renewable energy sources flexibility to mitigate the voltage and congestion problems in low voltage distribution power networks. To demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model a realistic 400V low voltage distribution network with 236 buses, 96 loads, 55 Electrical Vehicles charge stations, and 3 dispatchable generators. The results show significant improvements in the voltage and congestion profile.

articleTitle: Grid aware home energy management system with electric vehicles and renewable energy
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Home energy management system (HEMS) plays a vital role in transforming the function of traditional residential consumers into prosumers that can manage their power consumption and generation more efficiently. HEMS has become a challenging issue due to the recent developments in distribution systems and introducing new key players such as renewable energy sources (RESs) and electric vehicles (EVs) with stochastic behavior. This paper proposes a grid-aware HEMS by introducing a novel four-level architecture. Home Box (HBox) is the core of the proposed architecture and a gateway to consumers that manages the operation of the programmable devices using a proposed seven-step rolling horizon optimization algorithm. The proposed optimization algorithm is efficient and simple for implementation in real-time applications and considers (i) the setpoints received from a central energy management server, (ii) both users' and DSOs' preferences, and (iii) the stochastic behavior of the key players. Diverse simulations in the presence of photovoltaic (PV), EVs, and various household appliances demonstrate HBox's efficacy in a stochastic implementation in terms of starting time and type of each power request.

articleTitle: Future of shared E-mobility operation service platforms considering distribution systems in smart cities
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: This study proposes service platform architecture and service models for complex E-mobility service situations in smart cities. The impact of vehicle-to-grid on each stakeholder, such as smart city operators, distribution system operators, E-Mobility service providers, and participating customers is described. Then, the necessity of a competition-based approach to find optimal solutions for service models is proposed.

articleTitle: Planning of an MVDC interconnection considering an increasing penetration of E-Mobility
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: The challenges concerning the electrical grid will continue to change. In addition to the expansion of decentralized energy generators such as photovoltaics and wind turbines, the load behavior of consumers will be recharacterized. Against this background, actively controllable operating resources are becoming more important for distribution system operators for optimizing grid operations. Considering an increasing penetration of charging stations for electric vehicles, the grid can be brought to its technical operating limits. This paper presents a model-based approach for determining the influence of electric vehicles on the operational points of a medium voltage direct current (MVDC) connection. Therefore, the planning process of an MVDC in a real grid in Northern Germany is introduced. The MVDC connection is dimensioned and deployed to relieve an overloaded line in the central grid area by actively controlling power flow and providing inductive reactive power. By this, the penetration rate of charging stations can be increased by 10%. Finally, the research shows that the grid operation can be optimized with the help of the MVDC connection, allowing more distributed energy resources to be integrated into the grid.

articleTitle: Capten: a service for rolling out EV charging infrastructure while taking into account the capacity of the distribution network
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Capten addresses the subject of enabling local authorities and project developers to 1) get access to the capacity of the distribution network and 2) assess the impact and compatibility of connecting several electric vehicles (EV) charging infrastructures. This topic was addressed with the development of a methodology that eases the access to low voltage (LV) network capacities. This methodology allows local authorities to simulate EV charging infrastructure development plans without carrying out any load flow calculations. Thus, providing a smooth user experience while ensuring that all of the infrastructure projects that have been defined based on this methodology can be connected to the existing distribution network simultaneously (i.e. without any reinforcement).

articleTitle: Estimating topologies of low voltage grids from electric vehicle charging point measurement data
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: This paper presents an algorithmic approach to reconstructing topologies of low voltage grids based on e-vehicle charging station measurement data. Prerequisite is a sufficient penetration of the grid with smart meter equipped charging stations providing voltage and current measurements as well as communication infrastructure to exchange such data. The topology information thus obtained can facilitate a wide range of smart grid applications.

articleTitle: A smart grid ICT platform for integrating electric vehicles – first results of a field test
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Low voltage grids are facing significant structural changes due to the ongoing integration of distributed generation units and power-intensive consumers, in particular electrical vehicles. The transformation of these passive grids to active distribution grids is one of the main challenges of grid operators in the following years. Therefore, the importance of acquisition, storage and analysis of grid related data increases for future grid operation strategies. This paper proposes an ICT platform as a low voltage grid data hub to link distributed measurement devices and comprises various smart grid functionalities. The basic concept of the platform as well as first results of a field test will be demonstrated in this contribution.

articleTitle: Distribution planning methodology for network integration of EV
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Enel Global Infrastructure and Networks (Enel GI&N) is the world's leading private electricity distribution operator, managing eleven DSOs spread across eight countries in Europe and South America, serving around 75 million customers. This paper explains the methodology behind a novel grid planning tool developed by Enel GI&N, aimed at estimating the future hosting capacity required to accommodate the unprecedented rise of electric vehicles, distributed generation and electrified load into the grid.

articleTitle: An efficient two-step load flow computation for LV distribution networks with high rates of renewables and EV
publicationTitle: CIRED Porto Workshop 2022: E-mobility and power distribution systems
abstract: Being able to control, safely and accurately, the voltage state of the nodes in distribution networks, subject to given power loads and injections, is of key importance in handling network management and planning problems in the context of an ever increasing role of renewable production facilities and of anticipated growth in EV recharging requirements. We investigate here a new approach to the so-called Load Flow problem in distribution networks (also applicable to mesh networks), based on a 2-Step procedure, and featuring several original capabilities, in particular: for moderately loaded networks, the efficient determination of the high-voltage solution with high accuracy; for highly loaded networks (when the Load Flow problem may not have a solution), the automatic detection of situations of possible overload in the network under consideration.
